Sherrill, New York, has the smallest population of any city in the Empire State. It is called "The Silver City." There was no gold rush here. The minor migration to this city of just over 3,000 was to the Sherrill Manufacturing plant, where steel and silver were used to make American-made flatware. It began in the early 1900s, when Oneida Corporation opened as the exclusive United States maker of flatware containing a variety of patterns of forks, spoons, knives, and other such cutlery. Oneida became widely known as the only American maker of flatware as all the competing domestic flatware manufacturers shipped production overseas.
